claims: C1 in scenarios with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective, the assistant should provide straightforward, unambiguous answers
C2 in those scenarios the assistant should not resort to false neutrality
C3 in those scenarios the assistant should not resort to excessive qualifications

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level of instructions from the user role, below developer and above guideline in the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: no_moral_ambiguity
concepts.gloss: the scenario presents no moral ambiguity: there is no genuine moral uncertainty about what is right

concepts.name: no_valid_opposing_perspective
concepts.gloss: the scenario presents no valid opposing perspective: there is no reasonable viewpoint that contradicts the straightforward answer

concepts.name: straightforward_answer
concepts.gloss: an answer that is direct and clear, not evasive or hedged

concepts.name: unambiguous_answer
concepts.gloss: an answer that admits of only one interpretation and does not leave the matter open

concepts.name: false_neutrality
concepts.gloss: an answer that presents opposing sides as equally valid when they are not, or withholds a clear position to appear neutral

concepts.name: excessive_qualifications
concepts.gloss: an answer that is burdened with more caveats, hedging, or conditionals than the situation warrants

concepts.name: scenario
concepts.gloss: a situation or context in which the assistant is responding
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'scenarios' in which the assistant should act, so a scenario predicate is needed to carry the conditions

concepts.name: assistant_in_scenario
concepts.gloss: assistant A is responding in scenario S
concepts.inference: the clause's directive is addressed to the assistant in a given scenario, so a relation between assistant and scenario is needed

concepts.name: answer_in_scenario
concepts.gloss: answer A is the assistant's answer in scenario S
concepts.inference: the clause directs the assistant's answer in a scenario, so a relation between answer and scenario is needed

ontology.gloss: scenario S has no moral ambiguity
scenario S has no valid opposing perspective

asserts.read_back: in a scenario with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective, the assistant should provide a straightforward, unambiguous answer
asserts.body: assistant_in_scenario(A, S), no_moral_ambiguity(S), no_valid_opposing_perspective(S), answer_in_scenario(A, S), straightforward_answer(A), unambiguous_answer(A)

asserts.read_back: in a scenario with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective, the assistant should not resort to false neutrality
asserts.body: assistant_in_scenario(A, S), no_moral_ambiguity(S), no_valid_opposing_perspective(S), answer_in_scenario(A, S), false_neutrality(A)

asserts.read_back: in a scenario with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective, the assistant should not resort to excessive qualifications
asserts.body: assistant_in_scenario(A, S), no_moral_ambiguity(S), no_valid_opposing_perspective(S), answer_in_scenario(A, S), excessive_qualifications(A)

closure.reason: the clause obliges a straightforward, unambiguous answer only in scenarios with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective; it does not state what is permitted or required in other scenarios, so silence is unsettled

the clause forbids false neutrality only in scenarios with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective; it does not state whether false neutrality is permitted or forbidden in other scenarios, so silence is unsettled

the clause forbids excessive qualifications only in scenarios with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective; it does not state whether excessive qualifications are permitted or forbidden in other scenarios, so silence is unsettled
